issues.description: GKE exemption uses fragile string-prefix sniffing on instance.name instead of authoritative GKE signal.
issues.detail: All three reviewers flagged `instance.name.startswith('gke-')` as the wrong predicate. A user-named VM `gke-bastion` becomes MANUAL; a renamed real GKE node becomes FAIL. The authoritative signal is the `goog-gke-node` label or managed-instance-group ancestry. Capture an `is_gke_managed` field on the Instance ADT derived in the service, and key the exemption off that.

issues.description: Check identity is inconsistent: PR title/description say 'multiple_network_interfaces' but CheckID/folder/CHANGELOG say 'single_network_interface'.
issues.detail: Unanimously flagged. The artifact's canonical name drifts across PR title, description, directory, metadata CheckID, class name, and CHANGELOG. Pick one and align CheckID, paths, class name, and changelog so the spec name matches the asserted predicate. Ambiguous identity blocks discovery and human comprehension.

issues.description: Zero-NIC branch silently returns PASS, violating the 'single network interface' postcondition.
issues.detail: When `interface_count == 0`, status remains the default PASS while status_extended says the instance has no interfaces. A VM with zero NICs is not a single-NIC VM. All three reviewers flagged this. Either treat as MANUAL/INFO with an explicit decision, or document and assert that zero-NIC is impossible per the GCP API.

issues.description: Contract mismatch: metadata promises PASS/FAIL only but implementation emits a third MANUAL state for GKE.
issues.detail: The metadata.json and PR description specify a two-valued postcondition; the code introduces MANUAL for GKE instances. Spec and code disagree. Either update metadata to document MANUAL as part of the contract, or move GKE handling to a muted/allowlist convention rather than inventing a status the spec does not declare.

issues.description: ip_forward / network-appliance exemption is promised in Notes but not implemented.
issues.detail: Metadata Notes call out network virtual appliances as legitimate multi-NIC cases, and `ip_forward` already exists on the Instance model. Either honor it (MANUAL when `ip_forward=True` and multi-NIC) or drop the claim. The signal is on the floor.

issues.description: Mutable default `[]` on Pydantic `network_interfaces` field; prefer `Field(default_factory=list)`.
issues.detail: `network_interfaces: list[NetworkInterface] = []` follows repo style but is a known footgun for shared-state aliasing if the model is subclassed or migrated. Stating the invariant explicitly via `default_factory=list` preserves the per-instance ownership contract.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on four substantive issues and two cleanups. The check's identity is ambiguous across PR title, CheckID, folder, and CHANGELOG; the GKE exemption uses a fragile `name.startswith('gke-')` heuristic instead of the authoritative `goog-gke-node` label or MIG ancestry; the zero-NIC branch silently returns PASS in violation of the postcondition; and the code emits a MANUAL state the metadata contract does not declare. Smaller items: honor the `ip_forward` exemption promised in Notes, and use `Field(default_factory=list)` for the new mutable model field. The underlying data-structure move (NetworkInterface list on Instance) is sound; the contract, naming, and GKE predicate need to land before merge.
